summary: All 14 discovered candidate interactions resolved to status=verified (9 ENGINE_EXACT/ENGINE_COMPONENT-tier, 5 RULES_VERIFIED with conditional=true for the Smothering Tithe group + Oboro/Talon Gates/Cradle at RULES_VERIFIED/conditional=false). INT-0001/0004/0005 re-derived from primary Oracle text (not Spellbook paraphrase): all require opponents declining Smothering Tithe's tax (conditional:true) and are mana-neutral at Spellbook's stated opponent-count minimum, strictly mana-positive only at 3+ opponents (INT-0001's real threshold is 3, not Spellbook's stated 2). INT-0006 similarly corrected: mana-neutral at Spellbook's stated 5-creature threshold (net = creatures-5), needs 6+ creatures for genuine accumulating mana; the 5-creature threshold does support infinite (free) landfall/phase-out repetition, just not infinite mana.
impact: Resolved - no remaining unverified candidate interactions block Gate 1.

summary: INT-0011's original candidate writeup claimed Derevi's combat-damage untap trigger 'scales with attacker count' (N connecting creatures -> N independent untap-then-retap cycles on Gaea's Cradle). Only the single-attacker base case was engine-verified; a two-attacker extension test failed ('Can't find available command - manaActivate' on the second retap, suggesting the second trigger's untap did not take effect as sequenced) and was not resolved within the session's effort budget for that interaction.
impact: The multi-attacker scaling claim is downgraded to 'plausible per the underlying rules mechanism (CR 603.2c, 603.3b, 117.3b), not itself engine-verified' in interactions/verified/INT-0011.json - it must not be treated as confirmed until a working multi-attacker test exists.

summary: User audit of commit 51bd25f (SIM-0013) found two problems with INT-0012: (1) a factual rules-text error claiming Clever Impersonator's own text says it 'becomes an artifact in addition to its other types' - it does not, the Artifact type comes entirely from copying Birthing Pod's own copiable Artifact type per CR 707.2; (2) a validation-standard issue - the executable-engine test reproduces only a downstream consequence (two literal Birthing Pod permanents, each independently activatable) rather than Clever Impersonator's own copy transition, but the record had been marked status=verified without distinguishing that from an exact reproduction.
impact: INT-0012 was overclaiming its own evidentiary strength - a future consumer could not tell, from status=verified alone, that this interaction's exact named transition had not itself been engine-reproduced.

summary: Final bounded interaction-discovery sweep (per autonomous-mode directive) targeting Survival of the Fittest, Deathrite Shaman, Minamo, Shifting Woodland, Enduring Vitality, Badgermole Cub, and remaining Delney/Kinnan/copy-target space.
impact: One new material finding: INT-0015 (Delney doubles Badgermole Cub's triggered mana bonus, +2G flat per creature-mana-tap). Minamo+Gaea's Cradle (bounded, once-per-turn untap, not infinite by itself) and Enduring Vitality (grants creatures a mana ability, a synergy not a discrete new interaction) reviewed and deliberately deferred as low-impact per charter guidance - logged here, not separately validated. Survival of the Fittest and Deathrite Shaman confirmed (earlier this session) to have zero Spellbook-indexed combos and no material new interaction found on review.

summary: sim/rules_engine/ had no general Python orchestration adapter (decklist in, game log out). Built one: sim/rules_engine/xmage_adapter/ (deck_to_dck.py + run_diagnostic_game.py + SubjectDeckDiagnosticGameTest.java), driving real AI-vs-AI games (ComputerPlayer7) through a prepared XMage checkout, hash-verified against the frozen decklist, with machine-readable JSON transcripts.
impact: Ran 7 real diagnostic games (results/diagnostic/) - 4x 2-player Commander Duel, 3x 4-player Commander FFA - and reviewed every event against the full defect checklist. Zero rules-correctness defects found. One adapter bug found and fixed (seed applied too late, see INFRA-0005 for the residual AI-nondeterminism part). 4-player AI reliability issue found and scoped, not fixed - see INFRA-0006.

summary: Re-running the diagnostic game driver with the same --diag.seed does not reproduce an identical game line-for-line, even after fixing the seed-applied-too-late bug (moved RandomUtil.setSeed to @BeforeClass, confirmed the opening shuffle IS now seed-controlled). ComputerPlayer7's simulation-based decision search appears to have its own internal nondeterminism (likely hash-iteration-order or thread-scheduling dependent), independent of the shuffle RNG.
impact: Diagnostic game records retain their seed for provenance and the seed does fix the opening shuffle, but a past diagnostic game cannot currently be replayed bit-for-bit for deeper offline analysis of a specific line. Does not block SIMULATION_READY_DIAGNOSTIC-era diagnostics (each game is still independently valid evidence) or Gate 4 manual inspection (each game is inspected as it runs). Would need patching XMage's own AI search internals for full determinism - a large upstream change, not proportionate to this phase.

summary: ComputerPlayer7 (skill 6) is dramatically more passive in 4-player CommanderFreeForAll than in 2-player CommanderDuel. Investigated per explicit evaluation order: (1) skill/search-depth tuning - confirmed real, free improvement (skill 10 gives ~40-70% more events/game than skill 6 on matched samples; skill 16 is no better than 10, diminishing returns past that depth given 4-player branching factor). Verified at a 20-game batch: 0 crashes/errors, every seat takes substantial real actions in aggregate (25-50 actions each across 20 games), though a given seat still shows zero actions in 25-50% of individual games.
impact: skill=10 adopted as the recommended default for 4-player diagnostic runs (2-player stays at skill=6, no problem there). This is a real, meaningful, zero-cost improvement, not a full fix - per-game passivity for some seats remains a documented, labeled AI-policy fidelity characteristic (not a rules/adapter defect - 0 illegal actions or engine errors in any reviewed game). Steps 2-4 of the evaluation order (other AI implementations, a project policy wrapper, patching XMage internals) were not attempted since step 1 met the stated bar ("four active legal players... not elite play") - see results/diagnostic/gate4a_4p_probe/README.md.

summary: In the GATE_4A_2P_DIAGNOSTIC 100-game batch, Pact of Negation's deferred cost ("at the beginning of your next upkeep, pay {3}{U}{U}, if you don't, you lose the game") appeared in 6 games; in every one of the 5 that reached the trigger within the turn window, the casting player failed to pay and lost. The rules engine executes this exactly per the card's printed text (CR-correct) - the AI simply doesn't bank/reserve mana for a mandatory future cost it creates for itself.
impact: XMAGE_AI_POLICY_LIMITATION, not a rules defect - explicitly not to be fixed by modifying rules behavior per the owner's instruction. Concrete, first-party evidence for why GATE_4A_2P_DIAGNOSTIC win data must never be read as strategic/matchup evidence: 100% of the batch's 5 detected wins trace to this single AI blind spot, not gameplay quality. Non-blocking for diagnostic purposes (the rules engine itself is correct); would only matter if a future phase needed the default AI to play competently, which is explicitly out of scope for now.

summary: GATE_4A_2P_DIAGNOSTIC: ran and reviewed 100 real deck-backed 2-player Commander Duel games (tymna-thrasios-treefarm-v1 mirrored, seeds 1-100, skill 6, max turn 12) through sim/rules_engine/xmage_adapter/.
impact: 100/100 completed, 0 exceptions, 0 chunk failures, 0 engine errors. Automated + targeted-manual review against the full defect checklist found zero RULES_DEFECT/ADAPTER_DEFECT/TRANSCRIPT_DEFECT. Confirmed correct in organic play: Force of Will's alternative cost interacting correctly with Veil of Summer's protection (LIFO stack resolution correctly defeated the counter), Birthing Pod's full cast+activate+search-restriction math, multiple fetchlands, commander casting. Found one systemic XMAGE_AI_POLICY_LIMITATION (INFRA-0007, Pact of Negation) - explicitly not fixed, per instruction not to alter rules behavior for bad AI play. Did not declare canonical Gate 4 complete (only ~100 2-player games, not the full charter Gate 4 scope). First systematic evidence at scale that the rules-engine/adapter integration is sound across real organic 2-player play, not just isolated interaction tests.

summary: Every real deck-backed game run today before this fix (GATE_4A_2P_DIAGNOSTIC's 100-game batch, the INFRA-0006 four-player probes) used the test harness's default gameOptions.testMode=true, which makes GameImpl.init() skip mulligan.drawHand() entirely (Mage/src/main/java/mage/game/GameImpl.java: 'if (!gameOptions.testMode) { mulligan.drawHand(...) }'). Direct probe confirmed handSize=0 at turn 1 upkeep under the old code path - every game was played from a genuinely empty starting hand, refilled only by normal per-turn draws, never a real 7-card opening hand.
impact: ADAPTER_DEFECT, found while building results/solo_baseline/ (SIM-001 SOLO BASELINE v1). Fixed: both drivers (SubjectDeckDiagnosticGameTest.java, SoloGoldfishSnapshotTest.java) now use a new executeWithRealHands() method (reimplements execute()'s short body with testMode=false) instead of the inherited execute(). Does NOT invalidate prior rules-correctness conclusions (interactions executed correctly whenever they occurred, independent of hand size) - DOES invalidate prior activity/pacing characterizations. Reran with the fix at reduced sample sizes (time-boxed): GATE_4A_2P_DIAGNOSTIC v2 (40 games, results/diagnostic/gate4a_2p_v2/) shows activity roughly doubling (50.6 -> 102.6 events/game) with 0 new defects; the four-player probe v2 (8/10 completed, results/diagnostic/gate4a_4p_probe_v2/) shows much more balanced per-seat activity. INFRA-0007 (Pact of Negation AI blind spot) confirmed to persist identically under real hands, strengthening rather than undermining that finding.

summary: SIM-001 SOLO BASELINE v1: STATIC/COMBINATORIAL (exact hypergeometric math) and ENGINE-GOLDFISH (real XMage solo games, state-based accessibility) layers built and run for opening-hand composition, mana/color availability, acceleration, commander accessibility, tutor/interaction access, deterministic combo piece co-location, Pod/Survival accessibility, and cards-seen-by-turn, per data/decklists/tymna-thrasios-treefarm-v1.json (hash-verified) and the current interactions/verified/ registry (15 entries).
impact: New findings: land count is 27/98 (27.6%), notably below the ~40% usual EDH guideline - not previously quantified. STATIC commander-castability approximations (land+color availability only) are materially HIGHER than ENGINE-GOLDFISH's actual observed commander-on-battlefield rates (e.g. ~27% at turn 10 for either commander, n=15) - confirms the STATIC layer's own documented caveat that it ignores real sequencing. POLICY-DEPENDENT items (mulligan quality, tutor targeting, combo execution) explicitly left unquantified rather than computed with the current default AI, per instruction not to let AI quality silently determine conclusions. See results/solo_baseline/README.md for the full breakdown and the INFRA-0008 defect this phase found along the way.
